data.title: bn-204: Add Apollo64 PNG sprite round-trip

data.body: [high] Make quantization scale with normal generated artwork. Every palette-selection round currently scans all 63 candidates; for each candidate it scans every unique source color and then rescans every previously selected color. That is O(H * 63 * K^2), where H can approach the pixel count. Reproduction on the committed debug CLI: a 256x256 ImageMagick plasma PNG with the default 16-color budget takes 45.88 seconds at 99% CPU. A modest concept/reference image is therefore minutes or effectively unusable. Cache each source color's current best error (and ideally candidate distances), then score a candidate with min(current_best, candidate_distance) so each round is O(H * 63), and add a nontrivial many-color regression/benchmark guard.

[medium] Enforce the 64 MiB limit against the canonical RGBA allocation, not only the decoder's native output buffer. For an 8-bit grayscale PNG, output_buffer_size is one byte per pixel, so an image just under this check allocates an additional pixels*4 RGBA vector (up to 256 MiB) at line 191 while retaining the source buffer. Import also decodes before rejecting target dimensions, making a wrong-size PNG an easy memory spike. Use checked_mul(4), reject RGBA bytes over MAX_DECODED_PNG_BYTES before allocation, and test a header whose native size passes but RGBA size exceeds the cap.

[medium] Use the repository's standard format resolution for the new report commands. Both quantize and sprite import hard-code pretty output even when stdout is piped, ignore FORMAT, and reject the required hidden --json alias. Reproduced: piped quantize starts with multi-line pretty JSON; adding --json exits 2. The applicable CLI convention requires explicit flag/--json, then FORMAT, then TTY auto-detection (text for agents/pipes). Reuse the playtest OutputFormat/resolve_format path or extract it as shared plumbing, and cover piped/default, FORMAT, and --json behavior.

data.reason: Apollo64 quantization is pathologically slow on ordinary many-color art (45.88s for 256x256/default settings), the PNG safety cap permits up to a 256 MiB canonical RGBA allocation, and the new report commands bypass required format auto-detection/--json behavior. See th-gtdq8u, th-2n0dw4, and th-24p36l.

data.body: Fixed in 15958cd: quantization now snaps source pixels into at most 63 weighted Apollo bins and greedily scores only that fixed set, with a 2 MiB exact RGB bitset instead of a source-color tree. The reviewer's 256x256/default-16 plasma case is now 0.66s versus 45.88s (~69x faster), with a 256x256 many-color regression test.

Fixed in 15958cd: checked width*height*4 and enforce the 64 MiB limit against canonical RGBA bytes immediately after read_info, before decoder/output allocations. Added overflow-safe arithmetic and a regression covering a grayscale-sized header whose native buffer fits but RGBA expansion exceeds the cap.

Fixed in 15958cd: quantize/import now resolve explicit --format or --json, then FORMAT, then TTY-aware pretty/text output. Added integration coverage for --json and FORMAT=json; updated help, spec, and command references.

[medium] Preserve the promised report fields in the new agent-default text format. After fixing TTY detection, a piped/default quantize report now omits selected_indices entirely (repro output only has source_colors, output_colors, transparent_pixels, and MSE), despite SPEC saying the command reports the selected indices. The same shared filter drops sprite import's palette_indices, partial_alpha_pixels, changed_rows, alpha_threshold, and dry_run, although docs promise changed rows and surviving partial-alpha reporting. Text is specifically the agents/scripts format, so requiring --json to recover core results defeats the format contract. Print the command-relevant arrays/scalars in deterministic text form and add default-pipe assertions. Separately, remove --json from usage/spec/reference text: AGENTS' CLI convention defines it as a hidden alias, even though accepting it is correct.
